name: Rangrez Bandhani Ghar
address: First floor, inside a lane off Johari Bazaar, Old City, Jaipur
landmark: Turn into the lane beside the steel-utensil shop, climb the green staircase. You'll hear the radio before you see the shop.
about: A small family workshop-cum-shop. Shabnam ji will happily show you a half-tied dupatta and let you try one knot. Spoiler: it's harder than it looks.

name: Laheriya Lane Chunri Kothi
address: Shop in the inner row, Bapu Bazaar, near Sanganeri Gate side, Jaipur
landmark: Third shop after the bangle stall with the red awning. Look for wave-striped turbans hanging at the door.
about: Best for laheriya, the diagonal 'wave' cousin of bandhani. Meera ji rolls and ties the cloth herself and explains every colour bath.

name: Bindu Bandhej Haveli
address: Ground floor of an old haveli, south end of Johari Bazaar, Jaipur
landmark: Opposite the jewellers' row, under the pink arch with a peeling blue door. Pooja greets everyone with chai.
about: A three-generation family with a quiet back room for trying on. Pooja speaks French from her college days and loves explaining dot sizes.

name: Chhapa Ghar Sanganer
address: Printers' lane, near the old town gate, Sanganer, Jaipur
landmark: Follow the long white sheets drying on the rooftops. It's the courtyard with the neem tree and the stacked wooden blocks.
about: You can watch printing on the long tables in the courtyard. Ramesh ji's floral buti blocks are a joy, and Sunil carves new ones in the corner.

name: Dabu Dhara Bagru
address: Chhipa Mohalla, Bagru village, on the Jaipur–Ajmer road side
landmark: Ask anyone for the indigo vats. It's the blue-stained gate after the small Hanuman temple.
about: Earthy natural dyes and the famous mud-resist. Gopal ji speaks little English but his hands do the talking. Bring the phrasebook.

name: Neel Buti Prints
landmark: Between the brass-utensil shops, under the indigo-and-white striped awning. Ask for the 'block wall'.
about: Handy if you can't make it to Sanganer. Farida prints in Sanganer and sells here; the wall of old blocks behind the counter is worth the visit alone.

name: Neela Kumhar Studio
address: Workshop off Amer Road, a short ride north of Zorawar Singh Gate, Jaipur
landmark: Turn in at the signboard with a painted blue fish. The kiln is in the backyard, the shop is the front room.
about: A working studio: you'll see bowls drying on planks and Anjali painting at the window. Prices are on tags, which we love.

name: Firoza Blue Art
address: Tripolia Bazaar, near the Tripolia Gate end, Old City, Jaipur
landmark: Small shop with turquoise tiles set into its step. Mind the step; it's beautiful and slippery.
about: Tiny shop, big patience. Salim bhai paints small pieces at the counter and will happily wrap things for a flight.

name: Amer Neeli Mitti
address: Old Amer town, lane behind the main bus stand, Amer, Jaipur
landmark: Walk down from the fort's lower gate past the step-well sign. Blue pots stacked on a wooden cart mark the door.
about: A good stop after Amber Fort. Bigger pieces here; they can pack carefully for shipping if you ask.

name: Sona Meena Karkhana
address: Second floor, karkhana building in a gali off Johari Bazaar, Jaipur
landmark: Enter the narrow gali next to the sweet shop with the giant kadhai. Up two floors; ring the brass bell.
about: A workshop first, shop second. Vinod ji will show you the back of every piece without being asked. Bills always state the metal.

name: Haveli Meenakari Works
address: Johari Bazaar, north end near Badi Chaupar, Jaipur
landmark: Look for the carved wooden door with tiny painted parrots. The shop is through the courtyard on the left.
about: Great for small, affordable meenakari: trinket boxes and bangles that won't scare your budget. Naveen learnt Spanish from travellers, and it shows.

name: Gulabi Kundan Kaksh
address: Johari Bazaar, south end towards Sanganeri Gate, Jaipur
landmark: Above the shop selling pearls on long strings. The stairs are painted pink; you can't miss them.
about: For a special piece. They'll talk you through metal, stones and making charges separately, which is exactly how it should be.

name: Mochi Gali Mojari
address: Bapu Bazaar, inner lane towards Nehru Bazaar, Jaipur
landmark: Rows of mojaris hang like bunting over the doorway. Mohan ji sits at the front stitching with a curved awl.
about: The real deal: you'll see the sole being stitched while you try on. Geeta ji does the thread embroidery at home and brings it in each morning.

name: Kasida Jooti Ghar
landmark: Next to the kite-and-string shop. In winter you'll spot the kites first.
about: Good for wedding pairs and made-to-measure. Give them a day and they'll fit it to your foot. Abdul bhai has a few words of French for every customer.

name: Rangeen Mojari Kothri
address: Bapu Bazaar, outer row facing MI Road side, Jaipur
landmark: Tiny shop under a hand-painted sign of two smiling mojaris. Opposite the lassi cart.
about: Bright, cheerful and very affordable. Lata's beadwork is neat and tight; check a pair from the back and you'll see why.
